## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin, and gaunt woman characterized by sharp angles without curves. Her dark hair, which shows streaks of gray that grow more pronounced over time, is styled in a hard little knot at the back secured with two aggressively placed wire hairpins. She has a lined face with sallow, faded cheeks, and can sometimes look tired.

## Personality

Characterized by a rigid conscience and a sober, sensible demeanor, Marilla Cuthbert approaches life with a self-contained and often stern attitude. She is a proud woman who is deeply undemonstrative, scorning any display of emotional weakness and preferring not to openly reveal her affection. In her dealings with children, she relies on moral lessons and aims to drill them into a tranquil uniformity of disposition, which can make her speech crisp, curt, or uncompromising. She also values practical independence, striving to give [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) a good education so she is fitted to earn her own living. In her community, she is celebrated for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine.

## History

Marilla Cuthbert, who in her youth refused to forgive John Blythe after a quarrel, lives at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) with her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md). Expecting to adopt an orphan boy from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia) to assist on their farm, she is shocked when [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) brings home a young girl named [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) instead. Though initially determined to send the unloved girl back, Marilla feels sudden pity upon hearing Anne's difficult past and agrees to keep and educate her. She disciplines [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) through various mishaps, including Anne's fiery outburst at Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) and an accidental mix-up involving home-made currant wine served to [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md). Over time, Marilla grows deeply fond of [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), coming to realize how much she cares for the girl when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) breaks her ankle after a dare. Marilla supports Anne's education, agreeing to pay for her extra schooling to prepare for the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination and later watching her succeed in winning the Avery Scholarship. Following Matthew's sudden death after the failure of the Abbey Bank, Marilla faces the prospect of losing her eyesight and selling [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). However, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) chooses to give up her college scholarship to stay at home, care for Marilla, and teach locally.

## Quotes

> "I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P29](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0029)

> "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P25](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0025)

> “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind P35](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0035)

> "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002)

> "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P4](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0004)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla initially intends to return [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to the orphanage after discovering a mix-up resulted in a girl being sent instead of a boy, but she quickly changes her mind to save [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) from being taken in as a servant by Mrs. [Blewett](../character/blewett.md). Taking on the role of Anne's mentor and primary caregiver, Marilla works to raise her properly, instructing her in neatness, religious prayers, and household chores. Though she finds herself disciplining [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) for her fiery temper and wild imagination, Marilla grows deeply affectionate toward her and allows her to stay permanently as a dear friend at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables).

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P8](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0008), [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P39](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0039), +23 more_

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Marilla and Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) are neighboring friends who frequently visit one another to exchange local news and share tea. Marilla relies on Mrs. Lynde's experienced advice regarding practical matters and parenting, such as consulting her when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) refuses to go to school. Their relationship faces occasional friction due to Mrs. Lynde's blunt nature and strong opinions, particularly regarding the adoption of [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and Mrs. Lynde's outspoken remarks about the child's appearance.
